heading: PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Parigi Moutong.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Parigi Moutong.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in administering governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and organizations and/or community organizations.
7. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty;
9. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child
11. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of Violence.
12. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will or has occurred;
13. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the Victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against the Victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
17. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for strengthening Violence Victims to resolve the problems they face.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence to the family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Counseling is a process of providing objective and complete information, carried out systematically with interpersonal communication guidance, guidance techniques and mastery of clinical knowledge aimed at helping a person recognize their current condition, the problems being faced, and determine a way out or efforts to overcome these problems.
20. Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
21. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
23. Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Child Protection Service, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Child Protection Service of Parigi Moutong Regency.
24. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service provider institution for Victims established by the Regional Government.
25. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance as well as repatriation and social reintegration for Women and Child Victims of Violence.
26. Social Welfare Organizing Institution hereinafter referred to as LPKS is an institution or social service place that carries out social welfare administration for Children in conflict with the law, established by the ministry of social affairs.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to Victims in accordance with predetermined standards.

Article 12

1. Repatriation and social reintegration as referred to in Article 8 paragraph (1) letter g shall be implemented with the following principles:
a. voluntary;
b. safe and dignified; and
c. respect for rights.
2. In the event that the Regional Government is not yet able to implement repatriation and social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1), it may request assistance from related parties.
3. Social services to provide social welfare for children in conflict with the law shall be carried out by the Regional Government together with LPKS and other social institutions.
4. LPKS and other social institutions as referred to in paragraph (3) are rehabilitation and temporary shelter facilities for children in conflict with the law before repatriation and social reintegration are implemented.

heading: Article 13

Article 13

1. The Regional Government shall empower victims of acts of violence in the form of:
a. job training;
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups; and
c. capital assistance.
2. Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

heading: Article 14 Stages of protection for child victims of acts of violence, include:
translated_text:
Article 14 Stages of protection for child victims of acts of violence, include:
a. prevention of acts of violence against children;
b. handling of child victims of acts of violence; and
c. rehabilitation of child victims of acts of violence.

translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Prevention of Violence Against Children

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

1. Prevention of acts of violence against children as referred to in Article 14 letter a shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a network in efforts to prevent violence against children;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns with the community, private sector and non-governmental organizations; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of child victims of violence.
2. Prevention of violence against children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner and coordinated by the Regional Apparatus having the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: Article 24
CHAPTER VII
Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. The Regional Government encourages the business sector to participate in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. socialization to employees within the company environment regarding the dangers of acts of violence against women and children; and
b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

INFORMATION AND REPORTING SYSTEM

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

1. The Regional Government prepares and compiles an information and reporting system for the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. The information and reporting system as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

1. The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of P2TP2A.
2. Guidance and supervision shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus tasked with and responsible for the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
3. The results of the implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) must be reported to the Regent.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 29

Financing for the protection of women and children from acts of violence may be sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or
b. other lawful sources that are non-binding in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations that carry out protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 31

Activities for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Acts of Violence organized by P2TP2A before this Regional Regulation is promulgated, shall remain valid until the establishment of the Technical Implementation Unit of the Women and Child Protection Service by the Regional Government.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 32
This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by its placement in the Regional Gazette of Parigi Moutong Regency.

Promulgated in Parigi on

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PARIGI MOUTONG REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PARIGI MOUTONG REGENCY

NUMBER 15 OF 2018 CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PARIGI MOUTONG REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Acts of Violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Parigi Moutong Regency so that they are protected from Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of regional regulations. So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, so institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Parigi Moutong Regency.

Article 4
Letter a
What is meant by "physical violence" is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.

Letter b
What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.

Letter c
What is meant by "economic violence" is an act that restricts a person from working inside or outside the home to produce money and goods, including allowing a person who works to be exploited, while someone does not fulfill the economic needs of the family.

Letter d
What is meant by "social violence" is an act by a person or group of people that causes injury or loss of life to a person or may cause physical damage or damage to another person's property.

Letter e
What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter f
What is meant by "Domestic Neglect" is:
a. an act that results in the non-fulfillment of;
b. the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social;
c. an act of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of a child as appropriate;
d. an act of neglecting a person within the scope of one's household, whereas according to the law applicable to him or her or due to an agreement or contract he or she is obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person;
e. an act that results in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter g
Sufficiently clear
Letter h
What is meant by "threat of certain action" is any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
